text:
Sara: Heads-up — overnight BMC firmware push hit ap-southeast1 racks. OOB interfaces intermittently flap, a few nodes toggled secure-boot to 'enabled' unexpectedly. Provisioning failures for ~120 GPUs, scheduler marking nodes as degraded :warning:
Mike: Ugh. Any pattern on which SKUs or boards? logs?
Sara: Looks concentrated on r5-8 and r5-9 chassis. BMC logs show repeated "ipmi: session reset" followed by bios attr set change. Pasting snippet:
```
Jul 14 03:22:11 host36 bmc: ipmi_session: reset from 10.1.5.22
Jul 14 03:22:12 host36 bios: secure_boot_attr toggled -> 1
Jul 14 03:22:13 host36 provisioning: agent: lost oob connection
```
Mike: Can we hotpatch or do a rollback? Need to know impact on Dedicated clusters (reserved capacity). Product teams already seeing evictions.
Anita: Rollback runbook available. Steps are quick but need serial reboots to avoid mass eviction. Runbook snippet: run `oobctl rollback --image 2024-07-05-bmc` then monitor `oobctl health` for each rack.
Leo: Scheduler impact: roughly 12% of GPU capacity in ap-southeast1 marked unschedulable. If we drain aggressively we'll spike cross-region egress and interim cloud costs. Suggest draining only nodes with persistent MBMC flaps (identify via `last_oob_up > 5m` threshold).
Dario: For customer-facing inference, enable smart-routing fallback to eu-west/hosted tier for canary traffic. That buys time while infra does rollbacks. We have routing policy `region-fallback` we can flip to prefer eu-west for ap-southeast1 customers to avoid SLA misses.
DeployBot: Deploy started: 2024-07-14T03:10:00Z — bmc-fw-2024-07-14 -> ap-southeast1 (10 racks)
Sara: Confirmed one rack (r5-9) had a BMC reboot loop after firmware apply. Manual IPMI fixed it but secure boot flag stayed toggled. We need to ensure BIOS isn't forced to reset to enabled on next IPMI reset.
Anita: Quick mitigation: pin secure boot attr via `nvram set UEFI_SecureBoot=0` and add to oob policy until fw is fixed. That avoids re-provision failures. Also start a canary rollback on 2 racks now.
Mike: Cost note — if we start cross-region failover at scale, estimate added egress and burst Dedicated usage ~ $9k/day for the next 48h based on current traffic. Flagging finance.
Leo: I'll coordinate with scheduler to only evict pods on nodes with >=3 flaps in the last hour. Lower blast radius.
Dario: Also enable KV-cache warmup on eu-west nodes for active models to reduce cold-latency hit when routing traffic.
infra-oncall: I'm kicking off rollback on r5-9 and r5-8 canaries. ETA 22m per rack (serial). Rolling alert to @oncall-eng. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/bmc-rollback
Sara: Thanks — logging all affected node IDs to the incident doc. If rollback doesn't clear secure-boot drift, we'll escalate to vendor for microcode fix.
Mike: Keep me posted. I'll message Sales/CS about potential Dedicated impact and cost estimate.
Anita: After rollback, we'll run `oobctl verify --secureboot` across the fleet and then schedule a staged reapply with vendor-signed image.
Sara: Noted. For tracking: affected GPUs 118, degraded nodes 9 racks, initial deploy id bmc-fw-2024-07-14. I'll update thread with rollback progress and any billing impacts. :white_check_mark:
